findings.text: blocking: the `satisfied` branch of _section_target_satisfied is never exercised in production — the only producer of these rows, reckon/mcp.py:_resolve_plan_ref (lines 1836-1862, 'satisfied' absent), carries no `satisfied`, so every real row falls to the fallback arm, which calls _section_satisfied with a plan dict built from the row status and therefore takes the owner's `status in COMPLETED_STATUSES` branch; read_plan's verdict is unchanged in production and an undeclared section of a terminal plan still reads satisfied, the disagreement this node exists to remove.

non-blocking: the done_when asks for section readiness, progress and active sprint from the /_discover payload; only the section-readiness pair lands here, and the worker records the other two under outside_scope, so two of the four facts the goal names carry no guard.

non-blocking: the done_when's gate names tests/test_mcp_tools.py as a third file and the manifest's tests line runs only the two new-guard files, so the read_plan surface the production change touches is not in the recorded gate.

justifications.durability: tests/test_surface_parity.py:90 fails when _section_blocking is mutated back to the status read (negative-control.txt, 1 failed EXIT=1), but the guard supplies the roadmap's row shape with `satisfied`, which production never emits, so it does not protect the read_plan path; tests/test_producer_shares_the_classifier_verdict.py:222 asserts one classifier call per read across partition_live_runs, in_flight_by_plan and interrupted_by_plan and would fail if a surface re-derived, but exercises the shared helper and wrappers rather than the three named surfaces.
justifications.evidence: manifest.md:11 records a two-file gate omitting tests/test_mcp_tools.py, and baseline-head.txt records 23 passing tests at base, so the new guards never ran against the base revision as the done_when requires; the head and mutation logs do carry honest EXIT lines; evidence ends EXIT=0 and negative-control.txt ends EXIT=1 with a named failing id.
justifications.fit: reckon/mcp_views.py:2661 takes a function-local import of reckon.roadmap._section_satisfied, which sidesteps the module-level cycle (reckon/roadmap.py:90 imports from mcp_views) at the cost of reaching into a private symbol across modules.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/mcp_views.py:2656-2666 is reached in production only through the fallback, and because reckon/mcp.py:_resolve_plan_ref supplies no `satisfied`, read_plan's section_blocking publishes the same verdict as before the change.
justifications.reuse: The capability search found the owner already present as _section_satisfied at reckon/roadmap.py:659 and section_readiness_verdict at :908; the added _section_target_satisfied delegates to the former rather than restating the status set, so it extends the owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff 43a85b81..02e72411 touches only the three granted code/test paths and the declared evidence fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/.
